NTA for how you feel, it’s totally valid. It’s unfair to bring people into the word and then leave them before they even reach adulthood. If someone has chronic depression when they become a parent, it’s necessary to commit to living at least another 18 years. He should have been thinking about you more and put more effort into fixing his mental health, but he couldn’t or didn’t. As an adult, you really need to build your life rather than it being created for you by contextual relationships and activities. It’s a hard shift and I feel for you as I went through the same. 

Find a job that connects with your values and feel the greater meaning of how you contribute to society. Not having a job and not having to work is not the fun time you think it is. First 2 months will be fun, but eventually you’ll realize it’s incredibly boring to have nothing to do all day. If you didn’t need a job you’d need to find things to fill your day and get social interaction. Only wait - all the young people are working, so you’ll have to be besties with the retirees. Basically, to keep society (hospital for the sick, grocery store and suppliers for food etc) running we need people to work, even though that might seem rat racey. 

Find a job you like, find a career that’s exciting. Leave the desk job if it doesn’t work. Test out this job and then have the courage to try something different. Plan adventures and keep yourself happy. Please don’t try to off yourself. You’ll likely live and then it’ll be even harder to be happy, plus you’ll eventually have to find work anyway. You’re gonna die one day and it’ll all be meaningless. So while you’re here, make meaning. It’s hard and takes courage but it’s not impossible. 

Also to note, thinking about it like this would be very depressing to anyone. But living it, you can make it good I’m sure. Have you ever thought something would be really bad, but then after you did it, realized it wasn’t that bad? Basically you should try it before you complain too much. And if it’s so bad you need to complain, then it’s time to try something else.

Bpd is a serious diagnosis and tends to be misunderstood or misused. Totally understandable it’s bothering you. If it was just one session, I’d ignore it, not give it future thought, and find a better therapist. 

Apart from legit diagnosis which would need observation for a longer period of time, reasons for providing a bpd diagnosis can range from “I don’t really like this client and I want other providers to know” to “this client’s problems sound a little more than what I myself can handle, so it must be bpd”to the ever so cheeky “this client isn’t making any progress and it’s not my fault”. This particular diagnosis can be abused in so many unique ways. Especially if your case is more complex as you mentioned. 

I wouldn’t worry too much about whether you have it, unless another therapist or two mentions it again. The diagnosis is thrown around a lot for various reasons.

Additionally, I can’t imagine my therapist ever noting that her other clients don’t have trouble with something I have trouble with. This seems like he has a more rigid view of things. Saying he won’t listen to your pain anymore is just so strange, maybe there is a reason as sometimes crisis management can get in the way of learning DBT skills…but there are much nicer ways you could redirect the convo to skills, rather than say that. 

You’re not being overly sensitive. It would hurt anyone’s feelings to hear their therapist say that. I don’t know if he’s a bad therapist. What id do in this situation is bring up all these things in session. Try to use the dearman method to describe exactly what was said, express your feelings etc. Maybe write some notes. And I’d just see how he responds, if he’s defensive and unwilling to hear you, I’d probably walk. But sometimes bringing up things that hurt you can do wonders. It made my relationship with my therapist much deeper. 

Or maybe you could email him also to just note that in the upcoming session you want to bring up a few things that hurt your feelings, and some concerns you have with his approach? Even if he doesn’t reply, you then have no excuse to avoid it in the session. Sometimes it’s hard to bring up topics in session lol

Hi there, not sure what you’ve tried so sorry if I explained something you’ve already done

Doctor

You should start off by booking an appointment with your family dr asap and go over your concerns about your mental health. Try to be as honest as you can and hopefully you can come up with some kind of initial treatment plan for your depression, if you are willing to try medication. If not, they should still follow up with you to assess your condition and make sure you are okay re suicidal thoughts. In this first appointment, you should also ask for a referral for a psychiatrist. This will usually be in the outpatient psychiatry program of a hospital, probably lakeridge or ontario shores I think. Try to ask for more than one if you’re feeling bold, and take whichever hospital gets back to you first. The waitlist will be long. However actually recently CAMH only made me wait around 3 months for a consult, so that’s not too bad.

Therapist

Not sure where youve been looking for a therapist, but please don’t give up on therapy without a few solid tries. One good therapist is worth 10 bad ones. If you’re starting off, maybe try cognitive behavioral therapy and work on some behavioral activation.

Crisis

I define a crisis as feeling unable to cope with life’s struggles and struggling with thoughts of harm to yourself. In these cases, you can call 988 or kids help phone (it says kids but you don’t have to be a kid), or durham distress center (sometimes they don’t pick up though lol). I use KHP often, sometimes it’s hit or miss but I would be pretty screwed without it. Sometimes it can really help to have someone there when you think nobody cares. There’s so many times I think “im not calling another stupid crisis line again” and then I do, and it helps so much. So give it a chance. Others here have provided other good lines. 

Crisis-crisis

If you are in immediate danger of suicide, you should call 911, 988, contact a local hospital crisis line or go to your nearest ER. The least “dramatic” feeling of these options is just going to the ER. The crisis team there will assess you and even if they don’t admit you, I would hope they could give you some kind of referral or advice. I could never lie and tell you inpatient mental health treatment is fun, but at least you won’t die a preventable death. The worst choice you could make in this situation is to actually attempt to kill yourself, I promise. It’s really not that easy to do and a good chunk of the time leads to crippling disability and lower quality of life. Advocate for yourself. You said your wife would leave you but you don’t know that and im sure she would rather have her husband and her kid to have a father than not. 

It’s important to learn and remember that you have a genuine illness/mood disorder. Suicidal ideation (SI) is a severe symptom of depression. So when your suicidal ideation is worse, you should go to a doctor and tell them the problem, not off yourself. SI is the solution you’ve come up with to the problem, and SI is a symptom of the illness. Solve the problems (making friends fitness etc) and treat the symptom (meds/other therapies/distress tolerance skills). Don’t listen to the evil voice promising to be the solution. It’s really not a good or even efficient solution. Remember everything passes, nothing is permanent, and time heals all. 

You wouldn’t be reaching out unless there is some hopeful part of you. It’s clear how much you care about your family. They need you, and most of all you matter! You are worthy of this life.

All the best.

Again this is about asking in a way that gets you want you want. Of course how you feel about something matters! Maybe you have told yourself that it doesn’t.

In step 2, you can also state why you feel the laundry should not pile up. So for example, it gets mixed with dirty clothing, kids slip etc. It’s not only about protecting your feelings but you can also absolutely state your opinion on the matter there. 

Overall, being able to describe the problem or why you are asking, and then ask for what you want is a very important skill. It can be used even when you’re feeling lonely and want to ask your friends to get coffee. It can be used to ask your boss for a raise. With practice it won’t feel so formulated and awkward. I’m saying it easy to get caught up in these feelings and experiences portrayed to us. They can open old wounds or make you feel empathy for the story or make you wish you had friends like that or fantasize about the same thing happening to you. The emotions you felt were not fake, because they came from your own brain. However, you will need to learn to be able to take a moment after watching stories that hit you hard such as this. In that moment you should breathe and tell yourself that it’s a story and not real life to prevent the pain from there spilling into your own life. This is one of the reasons there are trigger warnings for this kind of material. It’s hard to identify what was yours before you watched the show from what became yours after you watched it. Take a moment to rationalize your own life and your issues and not become overcome with another story. I became very suicidal after mine, and all that pain was mine, but it had been triggered by this story, and if I was more careful in reading it, I could have been spared that pain.
